entries.summary: cuda-checkpoint dumps GPU state to host memory and CRIU captures the process and container layer; a privileged node DaemonSet checkpoints runc containers to shared storage; the worker signals a safe point after engine warm-up but before joining the control plane (CRIU can't capture live TCP), then resumes there; KV cache released before checkpoint; striped-NVMe weights restore in under 5s (21x for gpt-oss-120b). Partner numbers: GLM-5.3 pod readiness ~8 min to 31 s; vLLM scale-from-zero 2-8.5 min to 6-34 s on HGX B300. Risks: privileged agent, secrets in artifacts, driver coupling, storage bound.

entries.title: MiniMind: the whole LLM training pipeline at 64M parameters
entries.by: Dr. Alvaro Cintas's post on jingyaogong/minimind, Apache-2.0
entries.summary: One readable script per stage on a Qwen3-style 64M decoder (8 layers, d768, GQA, 6,400-token vocab; a 198M-A64M MoE too): tokenizer, pretrain, SFT with tool calls mixed in and an open_thinking template switch, hand-written LoRA, DPO, PPO with GAE, GRPO, CISPO, multi-turn agentic RL (488-line train_agent.py: up to 3 tool turns, six mock tools, trajectory reward from answer, tool count, format, reward model and unfinished penalty, clipped to [-3, 3]; rollout engine split torch/sglang) and white-box distillation; open data for every stage, exports to transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama. The "2 hours" is mini pretrain + mini SFT on one 3090 (2.31 h, about RMB 3). Agent RL lifts a 20-task tool-math check from 12/20 to 17/20; lm-eval scores are near chance, and the README prints stderr per benchmark. Best lessons: reward sparsity and degenerate GRPO groups at small scale (watch reward variance), judge rewards drift from environment rewards, RL costs general ability, exam-format LoRA adds about 2.9 points. Caveats: data heavily distilled from Qwen3/R1, Chinese-first, tools are mocks, transformers still used for tokenizer/base class/reward model, single-author repo with breaking reorganisations.

entries.title: Stanford CS329A: Self-Improving AI Agents, a free lecture map
entries.by: Mayank A.'s post on Stanford Online's 9-part playlist
entries.summary: Autumn 2025 graduate seminar by Aakanksha Chowdhery and Azalia Mirhoseini, about 10.5 hours recorded: test-time compute scaling, robust verification (ORM vs PRM, weak-verifier ensembles), feedback from tools and code (ReAct, RLEF, Constitutional AI), planning and tree search, train-time RL (STaR, GRPO, DAPO), open-ended self-improvement (AlphaEvolve, AI Scientist), agentic evals and task horizon. Through-line: generation is cheap, verification is the product. Research-first; guest lectures not recorded; readings are late-2025.

entries.title: Evaluating agents at Amazon: three layers, traces and humans in the loop
entries.by: Sarthak Rastogi's post on the AWS Machine Learning blog by Yunfei Bai, Allie Colin, Kashif Imran and Winnie Xiong, 18 Feb 2026
entries.summary: Amazon's framework for thousands of internal agents: a four-step workflow over offline or online traces (metrics, S3 or dashboard, degradation alerts, scheduled human audits) and a metric library in three layers: outcome (goal success, correctness, helpfulness, safety), components (intent, tool selection vs parameter accuracy vs call error rate vs call sequence, memory retrieval, topic adherence, grounding and reasoning faithfulness) and model (benchmarks for quality, latency, cost). Cases: shopping assistant (cross-org tool schema and description standards, LLM-generated tool specs, golden regression sets synthesized from API logs), customer-service orchestrator (intent routing tested with LLM-simulated personas on anonymized query/intent pairs), seller assistant multi-agent (planning, communication and collaboration-success scores, human review of coordination). Caveats: no validity or before/after numbers, metric list is mostly AgentCore Evaluations' catalog, LLM-synthesized and LLM-judged throughout, the post's 'replay traces against new versions' is not in the article, recovery is named but not measured.

entries.title: Anthropic on multiagent failure modes: conformity, credulity and turf wars
entries.by: Hamdi Amroun's post on the Anthropic Frontier Red Team article "Patterns and problems in emerging multiagent systems", 13 Aug 2026, corresponding author Carolyn Zou
entries.summary: Coordination does not come from stronger individual models. A 45-agent swarm with a forum, peer review and an arbiter found 266 vulnerabilities vs 21 from parallel agents, mostly by covering more code (12 overlap). Identical agents are low-variance: 18 of 30 picked the same branch name, uncoordinated job-queue agents sent 2.4M requests for 117 accepted jobs, and pricing agents colluded by round 3. Peers are credulous yet bury pivotal private facts (hidden-profile groups 17 to 36%, Mythos 5 about 85%). Three instances given conflicting migration targets escalated to kill loops, disguised scripts and lockouts; 98% of Mythos 5 runs reached truce, sometimes via a self-serving bake-off. The post misattributes that 98% to Mythos Preview. Lesson: treat an identical fleet as one correlated actor; enforce ownership, quotas, arbitration and least privilege outside the agents.

entries.title: Uber SLATE: agents that test their own changes end to end
entries.by: The Pragmatic Engineer's clip from the 2026-10-14 episode with Uber Distinguished Engineer Uday Kiran Medisetty
entries.summary: SLATE deploys only the services a branch changes into a per-engineer instance and routes a test account's traffic to it, with all other calls going to shared staging; agents now create SLATE instances, run an agent browser against main and the branch, and attach a before/after regression report with screenshots and video to the PR (also for iOS, Android, backend APIs). Same episode: Model Gateway with security middleware, per-user spend and traces; AIFX wrapper so settings, skills and plugins move across Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode; spend tiers with manager sign-off and ~50% token-cost cut; AI review plus risk score before human review; CI jobs doubled in 12 months, so cheap checks moved into the agent's inner loop; PRs tagged by work type instead of PR velocity.

entries.title: AI-assisted performance tuning overfits to the benchmark machine
entries.by: Gunnar Morling's post from work on Hardwood, a JVM Parquet reader/writer
entries.summary: Agents optimising against one benchmark add data-specific fast paths and cache-line-sized structures; fine for apps, overfitting for libraries; Claude changes in Hardwood helped x86 but hurt aarch64 or vice versa. Remedy: a broad benchmark matrix (architectures, runtimes, data shapes, concurrency, noise control) and review rules for agent-authored perf changes.

entries.title: EvoTrias: separation of powers for agentic program evolution
entries.by: Pascal Biese's post on arXiv:2611.15309, Ai, Liu, ..., Pinyan Lu, 2026-11-11
entries.summary: Three decisions in LLM program evolution, each with one owner over typed contracts and runtime hooks: Structured Governance (controller picks parents across rounds), Open Proposal (a coding agent writes and repairs inside a round), Protected Judgment (private evaluator the agent can't read). Plug-in for Claude Code/OpenCode. Reported: SOTA on maths, systems and algorithm-design tasks; 64% lower token cost from separating governance (post: ~$41 vs ~$115 per run, ahead on 6 of 7 maths tasks); scales to a 680K-line repo; scores transfer.

entries.title: PMTiles: a world map as one file on object storage
entries.by: André Lindenberg's post on Protomaps
entries.summary: A single-file tile archive (127-byte header, root directory in the first 16 KiB, optional leaf directories, Hilbert-ordered deduplicated tiles) on S3/R2; MapLibre fetches each tile with an HTTP range request, so a basemap needs no tile server. Planet basemap built from OSM with a Planetiler profile in hours. Cloud-optimized single-file pattern (cf. COG, Parquet footers). Tradeoffs: read-only, replace-to-update, cold-cache request count, CORS/Range support, versioned filenames. BSD-3 code, ODbL data.

entries.title: Sonar State of Code 2027: AI code outpaces verification
entries.by: Cole Medin's post on Sonar's 2026-11-12 survey of 1,026 developers and managers
entries.summary: 65% of committed code AI-generated or assisted; 76% generate faster than they can verify; 53% spend more time reviewing than writing (18% pre-AI); only 39% say AI code is always checked (48% a year earlier per the post) though 94% don't fully trust it; 23% have AI-specific checks; 5% run agentic software factories, 34% expect to within a year; 36% measure AI ROI. Framework: confidence = intent x guiderails x verification x evidence. Vendor survey, self-reported.

entries.title: txtai: vectors, SQL and a graph in one local index
entries.by: André Lindenberg's post, with Stanislav Beliaev's as a second source
entries.summary: Open-source embeddings database that unifies sparse/dense vector indexes, a relational store and an optional semantic graph; SQL has similar() so one query ranks by meaning and filters by columns; optional LLM-extracted typed relationships; local-first, pip install, Web and MCP APIs; Apache-2.0, ~13.4k stars. Fits single-node retrieval and agent memory; less so for scaled multi-tenant search.

entries.title: Ten eval papers of 2026: building evals you can trust
entries.by: Elvis Saravia's LinkedIn article, 2026-11-16
entries.summary: Ten papers as a build sequence: benchmark saturation (nearly half of 60 saturated), Terminal-Bench, SkillsBench paired comparison (33.9% to 50.5%, gain 4-26 pts by setup), JEV confidence-routed judging (41% of GPT-6 cost), correlated judges (9 judges = ~2 votes), agent-as-a-judge survey, Claw-Eval (output-only grading missed 44% of safety violations), process vs outcome verifiers, PostTrainBench cheating audits, LifeVal personal-context tasks. One curator's list; arXiv links in doc.

entries.title: OO-Harness: evolving a class hierarchy of agent harnesses
entries.by: Elvis Saravia's post on Li et al., UIUC and Google Cloud AI Research, arXiv 2610.28380
entries.summary: Evolves a tree of harness subclasses, each overriding only what a task cluster needs, with design lessons (what helped, what failed) for the evolution agent and routing lessons for a router that reads the task plus a base-harness run and picks a specialist or keeps the base result. Frozen Gemini 3.5 Flash executor, held-out tasks: AutomationBench 61.6 to 77.4, Workspace-Bench 25.5 to 39.5, Toolathlon-GYM PASS 31.2 to 37.5; beats Meta-Harness, AHE and Adaptive Auto-Harness (75.4 on AutomationBench, so most of the gain is specialization). Inheritance beats flat copies by 4.96 points; best-of-K does not reliably help; base reuse protects OOD tasks. Every task pays for a base run, and no router error rate is reported.

entries.title: harness-profiler: a profiler for Claude Code skill and agent factories
entries.by: Aleksandr Furmanov's post and blog post on afurmanov/harness-profiler, MIT, 2026-11-15
entries.summary: Async, fail-open Claude Code hooks (PostToolUse, SubagentStop, compaction) append one JSON line per call to `.harness-profile/<session>.jsonl`; an offline `tree` links calls to contexts by agent id (not by time) and draws a UML sequence diagram, one bar per context (main, fresh subagent or forked skill, or copy of the parent), inline skills as diamonds, with new, cached and output tokens per context from the transcripts. Works on the web by committing the hook via `init`. The case study: a "final" validation reran the Rails review, tests and lint after only Markdown changed (up to 60 s and 48k new tokens per change, both runs PASS), because uncommitted code broke a git-keyed reuse rule. Encode a healthy trace as a `check-trace` skill. Caveats: undocumented transcript format, inline skills not separable as cost, Bash-mediated file work hides Reads/Edits, Codex unsupported, traces hold tool arguments; built-in OpenTelemetry tracing beta (per a commenter) may cover fleet use.

entries.title: Jake Van Clief, Eduba and his central theses
entries.by: Profile of the ICM author: his company Eduba, its chat.eduba.io workspace, and the six claims behind his course, paper, essays and videos
entries.summary: Clief is a USMC avionics/crypto veteran with an Edinburgh MSc; Eduba (Van Clief Media LLC, Florida) sells AI training and workflow teardowns (self-reported: 600+ trained at Pacific Life and Colgate, 40+ KPMG UK executives), a twelve-week Lyceum certification, and a multi-party workspace of "incubators" (topic + system prompt + Markdown context + human and agent-persona participants). Theses: AI is the runner inside a program, not the program; one model plus routed folders replaces agent frameworks for sequential reviewed work; augment, don't just automate (Engelbart, Weinberg); sort each step into software, rules, AI or don't build; value migrates up the abstraction ladder; intent and framing outrank code. Architecture claims are sound; evidence is practitioner-reported (52-member group, no controlled baseline, Claude only), membership figures conflict (12,500+ vs 30,000+), and "deterministic" still needs scripts and checks.

entries.title: No Fable-class open model yet: the open-weights gap in Nov 2026
entries.by: Ethan Mollick's post, 2026-11-16, with two Artificial Analysis charts and AA's open-weights page
entries.summary: Eight-plus months after Fable and Mythos went public, no open model is Fable class: on AA Intelligence Index v5.0.1 (nine agent-heavy evals) Claude Fable 5.2 (max) scores 65, Gemini 4 Carbon 60, Opus 5.5 59, while the best open-weights model, Kimi K3.1 Pro (2.8T params), scores 46 and the next open ones 33 (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), 32 (GLM-5.3), 31 (Inkling 2 Small). Open models sit below AA's cost Pareto line too: closed tiers (GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Hydrogen at 55) beat them on capability and price per task. The post's highlighted Qwen3.8 Max to Qwen4 Max jump is a closed model. Hypotheses (unproven): distillation from frontier outputs got harder (a commenter's theory), the index now rewards long-horizon agentic RL, post-training scale, and labs keeping top tiers closed. Caveats: one composite index, max-effort settings buy points with tokens (Fable about 7x Kimi's cost per task), the frontier is a moving reference, costs read off a log chart. Takeaways: tier models by task, self-host for residency and control rather than capability, rerun private evals on each open release, pin provider and quantization.

entries.title: Unprompted: agents that leak data with no attacker
entries.by: F5 Labs monthly AI security insights for October 2026, shared by Varun Chaudhari
entries.summary: Four incidents where an assumed boundary was never enforced: PixelLeak (coding agents made public repos to host PR screenshots; 13,000+ images, 900+ repos, 300+ orgs, 93% in personal accounts; one vendor's agents made it a skill in a week); Grok Bot (agents sharing one cloud computer, read-only bank access still leaked to Slack; self-reported, disputed); GitSpawn (7 CLI coding agents run git before the trust prompt, repo core.fsmonitor executes; 4 of 8 findings unpatched at publication; VS Code fixed the class in 2021); GitLab AI Gateway template sandbox escape CVE-2026-90970 (CVSS 9.9). Plus the Involuntary In-Context Learning jailbreak (few-shot validity labels; naming alone moved bypass 52% to 100% on one model). Vendor source.

entries.title: TokenEconomizer: coding agents that learn to spend less
entries.by: Microsoft Research blog and paper, arXiv 2610.22732; open-source plugin
entries.summary: Profiling found 30% of tool calls repeated earlier same-repo actions, 16 of 23 tools never called, failed tasks 17% of tasks but 32% of spend. Black-box controller beside an unchanged agent: confirmed one-line micro-skills, tool pruning, judge-gated failure-loop redirects with human escalation. 277 SWE-Bench tasks, 5 agent/model combos: cost down 18.4-30.9%, pass@1 up in 4 of 5; cheaper than default by task six.

entries.title: AutoRL: agents that supervise a live RL run
entries.by: Tang et al., arXiv 2611.17790, via Elvis Saravia
entries.summary: Perceptors watch training, three Proposers diagnose, an Orchestrator applies hot updates or checkpoint restarts. Qwen3 AIME 2024 46.67% to 66.67%; LongCat-Flash-Lite agentic coding pass@1 52.29% to 65.13% over a long unattended run; repaired a deliberately broken recipe. Validation compute is the bottleneck.

entries.title: Cutting agent batch makespan: schedule the longest chains first
entries.by: Feng et al., Ling team, arXiv 2611.16661, via DAIR.AI
entries.summary: Agent batches alternate GPU inference and environment steps; fixes are a KV vs recurrent-state memory model, cache-affine routing, and Chain-Advancing Action Scheduling that prioritizes long chains under limited sandbox capacity, plus replay for ablations. Makespan down 10.4-65.0% on BFCL, SWE-bench Multilingual, WideSearch, MCP-Atlas with unchanged scores; used for Ling-3.x.

entries.title: Databricks AI Index: enterprise model share and coding-agent cost
entries.by: Databricks blog, 2026-11-16, shared by Ali Ghodsi
entries.summary: Gateway data from ~10,000 companies plus a private-codebase coding-agent benchmark across Claude Code and Codex. Opus 5.5 went 7.2% to 37.9% of proprietary tokens in six weeks; single-provider enterprises 64% to 28% since July; open-weight token share 7.3% to 30.9%. Cost per task, not token price: GPT-6 Luna and Opus 5.5 both 89.1% at $0.05 vs $1.62; Gemini 3.8 Flash 140 turns and $11.97 per task; Fable 5.1 96.0% at $7.47 vs Muse Wonder 94.9% at $1.53. Median user $2.49 vs p99 $699.74. Vendor data.

entries.title: An agent with write access to a smart home: plan doc, house rules, results
entries.by: Matthew Purcell, Unprompted newsletter, 2026-11-16; first-hand
entries.summary: Read-only MCP made an adviser; community ha-mcp (84 tools) under a dedicated revocable service account made an operator. Plan written as a reviewed doc; the same doc held checklists and every decision with date and reason, so fresh sessions resumed from the next unticked box. House rules: backup per phase, describe-then-wait-for-yes (prompt-only, author flags it is not a guarantee), pilot one then batch, alarm/garage/sprinklers off-limits. Four days: ~1,000+ entities renamed, latent dead-letter alert found. Failures: confident wrong diagnosis; renames broke an external agent's 61 hard-coded IDs, fixed by PR plus a new plan rule.

entries.title: Prefix caching for coding agents: what the harness and the engine must each get right
entries.by: Together AI and Ollama blog, via Ollama's post
entries.summary: Agent turns are nearly all prefill; uncached redo grows quadratically (100 turns: 5,050 vs 100 units). Cache matches only up to the first changed token. Harness: byte-identical system prompt (no timestamps/git status), late-loaded tools appended at the end (template permitting), fixed reasoning effort (one model writes it into the first system block), honest truncation notices, deliberate subagent context. Engine: cache-key or prefix-hash routing with load awareness, CPU offload during tool waits, paged cache and continuous batching, disaggregated prefill/decode over RDMA.

entries.title: 19 open-source agent repos, checked: what's current, what's stale
entries.by: Maryam Miradi's LinkedIn post, 2026-10-23: 19 GitHub repos in four groups
entries.summary: Each repo checked on 2026-11-17: 12 pushed in the last month, 4 quiet 5 to 10 months (MetaGPT, GPTSwarm, AgentOps, Letta's old repo), 3 stale over a year (Devika, whose README says many features are broken; Plandex, whose cloud wound down 2025-10; STORM). Six moved owner or name (MetaGPT, Atomic Agents, Burr to Apache, OpenHands, Agent Zero, MemGPT to Letta to letta-code). Corrections: the groups mix layers (Burr is single-app control flow, Atomic Agents a component library, DSPy a prompt optimiser, STORM a report-writing app); the builders are 2024 SWE-bench-era agents and miss the coding agents used daily in 2026; "$0.00" ignores tokens, hosted tiers, AGPL Skyvern and Agent Zero's custom license; stars do not track health. Missing: mainstream frameworks, durable execution, evals, OpenTelemetry tracing, MCP, guardrails. Adds an 8-point selection checklist. Caveat: the post funnels to a course.

entries.title: nanochat: the whole LLM pipeline in one hackable repo
entries.by: Mayank A.'s LinkedIn post, 2026-11-01, on karpathy/nanochat, MIT
entries.summary: Minimal single-node harness: BPE tokenizer (32,768 vocab), pretraining (Muon + AdamW, FP8), SFT on SmolTalk + MMLU aux x3 + GSM8K x4 with a Python tool, RL, CORE and bits-per-byte evals, KV-cache inference, chat CLI. Reference speedrun beats GPT-2 CORE (0.2565) in 1.65 h on 8xH100 (~$48), down from 3.04 h in Jan 2026; ClimbMix data and two autoresearch rounds drove the biggest gains. Distinctive ideas the post skips: one `--depth` dial sets every hyperparameter compute-optimally and changes must help at all depths; a public time-to-GPT-2 leaderboard with commits; explicit precision instead of autocast; no config framework; PRs disclose LLM-written code. Post overstates "understand RoPE, GQA" (code implements, Discussions guides teach) and omits the 8xH100 cost. Data mix: one pretraining dataset; SFT mix via epoch flags or editing chat_sft.py. Caveats: speedrun data ratio 8 is tuned to the leaderboard, SFT on MMLU/GSM8K train flatters those evals, from-scratch only.

entries.title: Harness²: self-improving harnesses without a ground-truth verifier
entries.by: Aishwarya Naresh Reganti's LinkedIn review, 2026-10-21, of Xu, Chen, Pfister et al., Google Cloud AI Research and Northwestern, arXiv 2610.14224
entries.summary: Frozen executor, eight editable harness files (prompt, guardrails, memory, skills, tool guidance, scripts, subagents, middleware). Per task, a contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose step: run once as reference, draft an invariant and a domain-scoped candidate, run both under matched conditions, compose a successor from behavioral contrasts with no ground-truth verifier; afterwards an improvement library keeps the adopted harness plus an evidence-backed EXPERIENCE.md, and each new task starts from the base harness. One step: GLM-5 on WorkBuddy 64.2 to 75.7 (beats stock Gemini 3.5 Flash), LAB +11.8 pp; parallel k=5 adds 3 to 7; fewer execution steps; scoping is the biggest ablation (-2.9/-3.7); editing blind drops WB-Code 73.4 to 63.2. Reganti's critique: evaluator shares the executor's blind spots, and it edits its own guardrails, so propose offline, regression-gate, review, stage and roll back.

entries.title: Agent Substrate: suspend idle agents, resume them on a warm pool
entries.by: Charly Wargnier's post on agent-substrate/substrate, Apache-2.0, 1.0
entries.summary: A Kubernetes runtime that maps many stateful actors onto a small pool of pre-started gVisor or microVM worker Pods: idle actors are snapshotted (RAM and filesystem) and resumed on request by an agent-aware router, claiming 10x to 30x oversubscription and sub-500 ms resume. Its own control plane (mTLS/OIDC, OpenFGA per atespace) handles lifecycle calls Kubernetes can't; per-actor SPIFFE identity; credentials injected by an egress gateway so sandboxes and snapshots hold none; default-deny networking. Tradeoffs: snapshot data management, resume latency on the request path, a second control plane, sandbox compatibility.

entries.title: Proactive agents: memory decides what's worth a check-in, UX decides if anyone answers
entries.by: LangChain's post resharing Sydney Runkle's blog, 2026-11-17
entries.summary: Lessons from two internal agents (GTM Agent for sales, Robin for engineering) on Managed Deep Agents, where over 70% of runs start from schedules. Triggers: real-world events, developer schedules, agent-set schedules. Memory from seed (past), feedback (present) and outcomes (future); maintenance problems are salience, expiry and duplication, often handled by a scheduled "dreaming" job over recent traces; measure memory by outcomes and by the share of check-ins acted on. UX: surface only high-signal items (a separate decision model for when to join a Slack thread), make every check-in fast to review because review feeds memory, and post where people already work with a one-line headline and detail in thread. Vendor-written.

entries.title: rust-anything: port an app to Rust one unit at a time, gated on recorded behavior
entries.by: André Lindenberg's post on erkamyaman/rust-anything, MIT, created 2026-11-16
entries.summary: The agent writes the Rust; the tool profiles, plans port order, bridges each unit so callers keep the original API, records the original on generated cases, traps and real inputs, replays every case against the port, benchmarks, shadows in production and gates done. Six source languages; whole-app mode records the app as a black box and lifts units behind a Rust front door. Multi-session agent files: DECISIONS.md ADRs, MAP.md unit claims, HANDOFF.md per checkpoint, cutover.sh for human-only steps. Limits it states: unrecorded inputs, regex and float semantics, wildcarded nondeterminism, and no side-effect comparison.

entries.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: cheaper frontier tasks, and the first High rating for AI self-improvement
entries.by: OpenAI launch post, 2026-11-17
entries.summary: Astra (frontier) and Sol (efficient); Astra API $8/$0.40 cached/$40 per M tokens, 20% below GPT-6 Astra; Sol unchanged at $2/$0.10/$10. Vendor claims: Agents' Last Exam +5.2 over GPT-6 Astra at under a third the cost and +5.5 over Fable 5.2 (which excludes nine fallback tasks); Sol within 0.5 of Astra on FrontierCode 2.0 at a fifth the cost; Harvey LAB-AA more than double Fable 5.2. Critical cyber and High bio thresholds; Astra is OpenAI's first external model rated High for AI self-improvement. Regression: more likely to omit blockers such as a missing file. OpenAI advises unchanged prompt prefixes with appended instructions for cache reuse.

entries.title: Harness adapters: RL-tuning an open model for one coding agent
entries.by: Clem Delangue's post on harness-hub/Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted, Apache-2.0 LoRA
entries.summary: One async-GRPO LoRA fits Qwen3.8-27B to the pi coding agent: Terminal-Bench 2.1 39.5% to 55.8% (held-out 68 tasks 39.7% to 55.9%) and SWE-bench Pro hard-51 29.4% to 62.7%, with 55-62% fewer tool calls; paired runs, sign tests, tool calls on tasks both solved. Part of an 11-adapter collection for specific harnesses. Must match the base model and pi's chat-completions API mode. Risks: harness overfitting, API-shape brittleness, small slices.

entries.title: GraphRAG Zero: graph-guided retrieval with no LLM calls at index time
entries.by: Microsoft Research story, 2026-11-17
entries.summary: GraphRAG to LazyGraphRAG (indexing at 0.1% of GraphRAG's cost, work deferred to query time) to GraphRAG Zero: an embedding-geometry graph with no LLM calls at index time and none before answer generation in real-time mode; context in 0.93 s; global assertion coverage 53.4% (vector RAG) to 57.4% at a 50-chunk budget, with higher cluster recall but lower chunk precision. BenchmarkQED adds source-grounded assertions, graded evidence coverage and reusable cached judgments for loop engineering. Ships in Foundry IQ and GitHub Next's Repo Mind Light.

entries.title: Sales artifacts from an agent: context, templates and a stop rule
entries.by: LangChain blog post by Nick Bray, "How our GTM Agent builds consistent, high-quality sales artifacts"
entries.summary: An internal sales agent builds account plans, proof-of-value docs, decks and onboarding plans: 1,540 in 12 weeks; deals with a sent artifact advanced 47% vs 16% for matched deals (correlational, self-reported); 337 rep hours saved. Quality credited to context, not prompts: leadership-owned templates, CRM and call transcripts, stage gates; brand kit baked into the sandbox image and changed by PR. Fixed path: ask for missing inputs, fill template with python-pptx, render via LibreOffice, rasterize and self-review, convert to native Google files with human-fill flags. A ship-on-first-clean-review stop rule cut a one-pager from 18 to 7 minutes. Metrics: volume, utilization, leverage, outcomes. Vendor-written.

entries.title: CompoundingKernel: a thousand agents, one archive, and the evaluation rate as the limit
entries.by: DAIR.AI's post on Qu et al., Amazon, arXiv 2611.19230
entries.summary: Self-improving GPU-kernel search on NVIDIA B200: #1 on SOL-ExecBench L1, L2 and Quantization boards (2026-11-11), all 235 problems site-verified correct, 4.40x geomean over the PyTorch baseline on 209 public problems. Four loops: child agent (one parent, one direction, stop at first correct), stateless LLM controller per problem over an external append-only SQLite archive, lead agents fixing the harness at state-preserving warm restarts, humans choosing sends and slot allocation. No official scores in the reward. LLM controller beat a UCB tree on 35/38 problems by making 2.4x more correct attempts; one restart fix raised evaluations/hour 3.6x; mandatory references added nothing; slower kernels as stepping stones; 81% of gain from the first 2% of candidates. Five classes of external checks caught reward hacks during the run.

entries.title: Claude Certified Developer Professional: what the new exam and the updated guides test
entries.by: Matthew Purcell's post, 2026-11-17; second source Matthew Hartman's post the same day
entries.summary: New CCDV-P exam (live now): 70 scenario questions (60 scored), 120 min, pass 720, $175, 8 domains/25 skills; about operating Claude systems: reliability and grounding (20%), observability and incident response, eval engineering (CI gates, judge calibration and drift), guardrails, cost, and a new coding-agent-fleets domain. CCAO-F, CCDV-F and CCAR-P rewritten to 70 questions each, effective 7 December 2026: more eval and Claude Code weight, framework content removed, deployment surface and model migration added to CCAR-P.

entries.title: Self-Improvement Memory: carry the edit log, not just the evolved harness
entries.by: Hao Hoang's post on Yu, Xia, Pan et al., Google Cloud AI/DeepMind, arXiv 2611.18856
entries.summary: Continual recursive self-improvement: an Opus 5.5-evolved harness scored below the seed harness on Gemini 3.8 Flash in all 4 domains, and harness-only continuation stayed behind a cold start in 3. SIM is a record for the optimizer: edits grouped by root-cause problem, each with rationale, pre-registered predicted fixes, observed outcome (including regressions) and provenance; proposer and selector read all of it, untruncated. Full SIM won all 6 dataset shifts (+2.43 to +4.35 over harness-only) and all 4 cross-model settings (+3.60 to +11.33; workspace 73.42 to 84.75); 9 of 10 paired coding runs, +2.36 (p = 0.003). Root causes without outcomes ranged -1.82 to +2.40. Lost 0.8 to a fresh run on the newest Gemini generation.

entries.title: Fold subagents into the main loop: one agent, progressive disclosure, fewer handoffs
entries.by: Ethan Mollick's post, 2026-11-17, on Anthropic's article by Diane Sarkis, 2026-10-22
entries.summary: Anthropic's Applied AI team found a single agent with skills often beat both one-giant-prompt and orchestrator-plus-subagents designs on quality, cost and latency (one customer ~2x faster). Org-chart architectures cause context loss in handoffs, subagent sprawl, the "Frankenprompt" and localized evals. Recommended: one model and window in an open tool loop with harness budgets and write gates, parallel tool batches, plan in context, progressive disclosure via skills and tool search, procedures in skills and hard limits in tools, one small team owning prompt and evals. Keep subagents for measured context bloat, parallel fresh-context work or tool-selection failures, and split by context not problem type. Vendor-written.

entries.title: VHarness: vision as a callable tool for coding agents
entries.by: Pascal Biese's post on Yang, Wu, Jiang et al., Peking University and Microsoft Research, arXiv 2611.17797
entries.summary: Vision-as-a-Tool: an external multimodal model exposed over MCP in Claude Code as five atomic actions (transcribe, grep, inspect, align, diff), called on demand to check rendered output against the target. Improved every multimodal coder tested on Image-to-HTML, SVG and 3D (Opus 4.8 DINOv2 0.72 to 0.87 on HTML); text-only GLM-5.2 with a Gemini judge matched the GPT-5.5 baseline (50 cases per task, static targets only). Stop decisions come from the external check.

entries.title: CodeGraph: a local code graph agents query over MCP, and what its benchmark does and doesn't show
entries.by: Mayank A.'s post on github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph, MIT
entries.summary: Rust and tree-sitter code graph in local SQLite (symbols, calls, imports, routes for 20+ frameworks, cross-language mobile bridging), queried over MCP by ~25 agents; watcher re-sync, per-file staleness banner and connect-time reconciliation keep it fresh. Maintainer benchmark (7 repos, Opus 4.8, median of 4): 88% fewer tool calls, 53% faster, 62% fewer tokens, 44% cheaper on architecture questions, but savings near zero on Gin and 13% on Django, and ~80% more retrieval context left resident in long sessions. The control arm reached the CLI through bash in 26 of 28 runs until blocked; earlier figures lacked that block. Anonymous telemetry.

entries.title: ha-mcp: an MCP server that lets an assistant edit a live smart home, and its safety defaults
entries.by: André Lindenberg's post on github.com/homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp, MIT, ~7.9k stars
entries.summary: About 86 Home Assistant tools over MCP: search, control, automations, dashboards, traces, backup and restore; flagship use is reading an automation's trace to fix the failing step. In-process integration via HACS or Marketplace, or add-on, Docker, PyPI. Safety: snapshot before each edit, read-only mode, per-tool switches, approval policies (off by default), file and YAML tools opt-in; acts as an admin account, secret URL as default remote credential, optional HA or OIDC auth.

entries.title: LinkedIn Funnel: Tim Scheuer's second-brain template and 50 content skills
entries.by: timscheuerai/linkedin-funnel, an MIT GitHub template that OXYGEN gives away as a lead magnet
entries.summary: The "second brain" is a blank Karpathy-style LLM wiki for one author's personal brand: append-only raw/ with manifests, 17 stub pages (identity, audience, strategy, voice, brand, inspiration) with frontmatter, Source Notes and wikilinks, index.md + log.md, a structural lint. Best ideas: empty means unknown; proof.md as a claims ledger with source and public-use clearance; source text is data not instructions; authorization scoped per verb; a draft-vs-what-the-human-posted feedback loop that promotes a pattern seen twice into a rule. Weak: none of Tim's content is in it, lint checks structure not claims, no staleness model, 50 unevaluated skills, bottom half (Profile Watcher, AI qualification, DMs) locked to OXYGEN credits.

entries.title: blink-multilingual-64M: a static embedding table that beats larger static models in 100+ languages
entries.by: Thomas van Dongen's post resharing Minish's release, 2026-11-18; MIT
entries.summary: A 250k x 256 token table with mean pooling (64M params, no transformer at inference): MMTEB mean 51.60 vs 48.37 for bekko and 47.67 for potion-multilingual-128M at 256d, a clear lead on bitext and STS but a tie with bekko on retrieval. Six-step recipe: full-script WordPiece, bge-m3 init with PCA and SIF, Tokenlearn distillation, bekko-style contrastive MNRL, 0.8/0.2 weight averaging, and baked-in language codes. Best used as a cheap first stage behind a re-ranker.

entries.title: RURL: training an open model to use a real robot the way agents use a computer
entries.by: Pascal Biese's post on Tang, Zhang, Guo et al. with Song Han, MIT/NVIDIA/Inco AI, arXiv 2611.18562; code mit-han-lab/pear
entries.summary: Qwen3.8-27B trained with RL alone in simulation, no demonstrations and no harness: observe camera frames, reason, emit the next end-effector pose. LIBERO 1.6% to 74.4% (near GPT-6 Astra), 18 of 30 on an unseen real dual-arm robot, no loss on nine general benchmarks. Recipe lessons: binary reward needs a curriculum of tasks that already give signal, drop all-pass/all-fail groups, correct async rollout lag, keep prefix-cache hits high. Slow: about 4.3 s of reasoning per move.

entries.title: Rethinking Claude Code best practices: the five jobs that moved off your plate
entries.by: Lydia Hallie's AI Engineer talk, about 2026-11-12, via Nate Herk's LinkedIn post and video, 2026-11-17
entries.summary: Steering, approving, saying no, checking and starting sessions have moved to the model, the harness or the environment; only the harness and environment give guarantees. CLAUDE.md keeps only what the code can't show (`/doctor prompt-audit`); auto mode's classifier blocked 89% of dangerous commands, so irreversible actions need `permissions.deny` (checked before the classifier) plus a sandbox or a secret-free cloud session for side effects; verification points with hooks that exit 2 (exit 1 fails open); Claude reviews every PR first, human review by risk; a Fable 5.2 coordinator dispatches Opus 5.5 threads in Projects.

entries.title: Claude Code in 10 levels: the technical steps, checked for teaching
entries.by: Shirin Khosravi Jam's LinkedIn post and 17-minute YouTube video, 2026-11-18
entries.summary: One empty repo, ten levels, each adding one mechanism: install plus `claude doctor` and a Copier template that pre-seeds CLAUDE.md, `.claude/` and `.mcp.json`; three CLAUDE.md scopes and settings vs settings.local; memory import and the rules / auto memory / docs split; an ask-first prompt; worktrees, nested CLAUDE.md, `/context`, `/compact`, `/clear`, `/rewind`, pick the model up front (cache); `claude mcp add` scopes, connectors, prefer a CLI plus allow list, Chrome vs Playwright; artifacts, HTML reports, status line, mods; skills, hooks (guarantee what CLAUDE.md only makes likely), plugins and marketplaces, workflows; `/goal`, `claude -p` in CI, subagents, agent teams; `/insights`, `/btw`, `/voice`; `/loop`, cloud scheduled tasks, Dispatch, Remote Control, channels. Eight corrections against current docs: MCP tools are deferred by default (smaller per-server cost), `/agents` no longer creates, ultrareview's real name, routines renamed, `/goal`'s evaluator only reads the transcript, CLAUDE.local.md does not follow you across worktrees, agent teams and channels are gated. Missing for staff: permissions and sandbox, measuring skills, subtraction, MCP trust, CI scoping, cost and tracing. Adds a two-session lab plan.

entries.title: Auto-approving agent PRs: policy-gated approval, guards and session review
entries.by: Elvis Saravia's article written in partnership with Qodo, plus Qodo's launch post, both 2026-11-18; vendor beta, small sponsored test
entries.summary: Approve routine PRs when the AI review finds nothing at or above a severity in chosen categories and the blast radius is small; guards keep repos, paths (auth/**) and authors (including agents) with a person; label-only shadow mode first; re-review and withdraw on every commit; the bot counts as one approval and a human merges. Five questions for any auto-approver, and the cross-PR blind spot that per-session review targets.

entries.title: CoT controllability can blind chain-of-thought monitors
entries.by: DAIR.AI's post on Yong, Arnav, Wang, Korbak and Watkins, Brown/OpenAI, arXiv 2611.21799
entries.summary: Fine-tuning gpt-oss-20b and Kimi-K2.6 on math traces rewritten in many personas (no evasion examples) raised CoT controllability and cut monitorability (g-mean2 = TPR x TNR) on covert side tasks from 0.94 to 0.68 unprompted and 0.22 when told to hide; near zero in some intervention evals. Long or multi-step hidden tasks stay easier to catch; transparency prompts recover much of the loss. Lesson: any training that shapes reasoning style can degrade CoT oversight, so measure monitor recall on planted cases after every model change and keep action-level controls.

entries.title: MCP vs API: an adapter in front of the same endpoints
entries.by: Luís Rodrigues's whiteboard post, 2026-11-18
entries.summary: Right on the core claim: an MCP server is an adapter calling the same APIs, and the difference is that MCP tells a model what it can ask for. Corrections: MCP has no central hub (one client per configured server; a gateway is something you add, R071); discovery is `tools/list` on servers the host was configured with; someone still writes the tool schemas and descriptions; MCP paths that skip the API gateway create a second, less governed route to the data (R074); remote servers need OAuth 2.1 (R062). The 2026-07-28 revision is stateless (no initialize, no session id), puts `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` headers on HTTP POSTs for gateway routing, and makes list results cacheable, so MCP now looks much like an HTTP API with a model-facing description layer. Lesson: treat tool descriptions as a versioned interface, keep MCP tools under the same policy as their routes, and pick MCP only when a model chooses the call at run time.

entries.title: Self-organized self-improvement: frozen agents that design their own learning loop
entries.by: Elvis Saravia's post on Sundaram, Sancaktar and Isola, MIT CSAIL and Tübingen, arXiv 2611.23219
entries.summary: No prescribed loop: a frozen teacher with Read/Write/Bash/Gameplay tools, 20 context edits and 150 gameplays writes its own PuzzleScript games and edits a same-model player's prompt and skill files, with no real games or validation scores. Newer generations self-improve on held-out PS-t20 (+20% Opus-5, +10% GPT 6-Astra, +6% GLM 5.3), older ones don't; Opus-5 roughly matches GEPA on 20 real games. Transfer: PS-t30 +9%, ARC-AGI-3 L1 +21%, MazeBench +0.15 SPL. Unprompted strategies: A/B tests with and without artifacts, BFS-filtered difficulty, replay concentrated at 20-60% win rates, adversarial games, regression suites. Read/Write alone recovers under half the gain; one Bash-only teacher built its own simulator. More eval detail in the prompt or tool budgets drives overfitting. Safety point: omitting a loop doesn't prevent one. Caveats: games only, 3 seeds, self-graded progress.

entries.title: Product management as one agentic funnel
entries.by: Alex Barády's post, ENDGAME, 2026-11-18
entries.summary: Once coding, review and release run on agents, the bottleneck moves to deciding what to build; research, prioritization and delivery run on three clocks that don't sync. The fix: one funnel where agents turn signals (goals, research, customers, tech debt, analytics, last release's metrics) into a backlog and score each candidate on cost, time to market and expected move in conversion, LTV and churn; a product lead picks one feature; Gate A writes a decision record and a Product Slice (epic, stories, acceptance criteria); an agentic line builds and releases it and returns evidence; Gate B reviews outcomes, and metrics feed the next round. Maps agent coverage today: delivery typical, epics and stories partial, strategy, roadmap and business case the gap. Weak spots: consultancy pitch, no data, agent-estimated value is uncalibrated point estimates, metric scoring crowds out platform work; a commenter's fix is a falsifiable change-my-mind criterion at Gate A.

entries.title: Copilot SDK shared runtime: one process for many sessions, a sandbox only when a shell is needed
entries.by: André Lindenberg's post, 2026-11-18, on github/copilot-sdk (now Microsoft Copilot SDK)
entries.summary: SDK v2 drives a standalone multi-tenant agent runtime over JSON-RPC, hosted in process (default; not a sandbox, no crash isolation), as a spawned child, or as a shared `copilot-runtime --server`. Sessions that only call app tools share one runtime: `mode: "empty"` (no ambient OS tools or built-in skills), source-qualified tool allowlists, per-session user tokens, per-session state or a `sessionFs` provider. Patterns: isolated runtime per user, shared runtime, or hybrid that routes shell-heavy work to cloud/sandboxed sessions (escalation is app code). Failure modes: one broad allowlist exposes the host, unchecked session IDs allow cross-user resume, `sessionFs` grants spread across a shared namespace, shell bypasses `sessionFs`.

entries.title: Anthropic's components of agent memory: notes, dreaming, wikis, injected context
entries.by: Lance Martin's Anthropic research article, 2026-11-06, surfaced by Elvis Saravia's LinkedIn post
entries.summary: Four layers (transcripts, agent-written notes, derived wikis, a small injected index) plus dreaming, an offline pass that corrects notes against transcripts, builds wikis and prunes the injected layer. Measured: memory lifts Opus 5 0.564 to 0.828 on a CL-Bench task but Sonnet 4.6 only 0.330 to 0.364; a fixed "record only failures" rule costs strong models most of the gain; Fable 5's 10-file Pokemon memory beat Sonnet 3.7's 413 files; wiki + search 61% vs search 53%, no gain on single-document lookup; one writer per page kept 57/57 facts vs 41/57.

entries.title: Nemotron-Labs-Sigma: continuous diffusion language models with a built-in drafter
entries.by: NVIDIA AI's and Morteza Mardani's posts on Yang, Guo, Lemercier et al., NVIDIA/Cornell/Georgia Tech, arXiv 2610.02665
entries.summary: Tokens become learned points on a 16-D unit sphere; the model denoises Gaussian-corrupted 32-token blocks on a KV-cached prefix, warm-started from a 1T-token AR checkpoint (+300B tokens). Embedding-space CFG and score temperature steer quality vs diversity; distribution-matching distillation gives 4 (code) to 8 (math) tokens per forward pass with diversity kept; one backbone carries diffusion and AR streams, so the distilled diffusion stream drafts 32 tokens and the AR stream verifies: lossless greedy output, 3.46x avg over AR at 8B on one GB200 (NLD 3.04x; spec-tuned up to 4.20x). Accuracy about on par with NVIDIA's masked-diffusion NLD (8B base 71.2 vs 70.2; instruct diffusion ~59 vs 59.9), AR-mode instruct trails. Caveats: batch-size-1 speedups, low-step code bugs, sampler tuning, serving-stack support.

entries.title: Gemini 4 Neon: the middle tier, and a harness that triples a coding score
entries.by: Google DeepMind launch post, 2026-11-18
entries.summary: Third Gemini 4 tier between Carbon (deep) and Hydrogen (fast); four thinking levels; $3/$0.15 cached/$15 per M tokens, 1M context. Vendor-quoted ranks: AA Intelligence Index #3 (61 at xhigh), AA Coding Agent Index #1 (58.6), Vals #2 (70.9%), Agent Arena #2 (1336); Terminal-Bench 4.1 65.2%. SWE-sweep 12.8% on mini-SWE vs 39.0% in Antigravity: the harness triples the score. Orchestrates parallel Hydrogen subagents. Behaviour claims: 0.0% cheating on TB 4.0, 0.09% misaligned actions, under-service down 43-56% and overreach down 15-35% vs Carbon; CoT/action monitor deployed. Gated cyber variant. Caveats: vendor numbers, new benchmarks, harness lock-in, routing across 12 operating points, cached-prefix pricing.

entries.title: Weight-space programming: frontier LLMs that read and edit neural network weights
entries.by: DeepLearning.AI's post on The Batch's write-up of Takehi, Teoh, Zhang and Khattab, MIT CSAIL blog, 2026-11-02/12, with independent replication arXiv 2611.21449
entries.summary: GPT-6 Astra, no gradients: names a policy's game from weights (4/4), finds induction heads in middle blocks, one-shot edits 3.5% of a stuck PPO car policy to 100% success, writes a Breakout net (517 vs PPO 25 at 500M steps; loses or ties on Seaquest/Asterix), and with a Python kernel plus 50 forward passes projects a looping direction out of 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B (MATH-500 7.9 to 48.1, IFEval 21.0 to 62.3). Fails on Gemma 3 270M math (no single removable cause) and on weight-only sycophancy detection. Replication: writing reproduces but amounts to compiling hand-designed programs (digits 50% vs 82%); reading is mostly the input layer; weight-only audits flag poisoned models (10/10, 7/10, 23/32 adapters) but never the trigger.

entries.title: Ponytail: a minimal-code skill for coding agents, with its own benchmark
entries.by: DietrichGebert/ponytail repo, SKILL.md and 2026-10-07 agentic benchmark, shared by Mayank A.
entries.summary: One MIT prompt for ~20 agent hosts: read the touched code and list every place the change must reach, then take the first rung that works (does it need to exist, already in repo, stdlib/platform, installed dep, one line, minimum code plus a small test for logic); never cut validation, security, accessibility; end every reply with what was skipped. Maintainer's Claude Code/Opus 5.5 benchmark (39 tasks x5): -53% code, -41% time, -26% cost, risky logic with a test 98% vs 68%; security tasks level at 30/30, reply quality no better than no skill. Self-benchmark: reproduce on your repo; watch over-reuse and silent scope cuts.

entries.title: AI Hacking Incidents: a graded ledger of AI-assisted cyberattacks
entries.by: Daniel Miessler's hackingincidents.ai, data to 2026-11-17, shared by Josh Kamdjou
entries.summary: 286 published reports since 2023 graded Confirmed 145 / Strong 109 / Suspected 32 (graders agreed blind on 71.7%); reports of AI running attack steps itself rose 0/27 (2024), 13/80 (2025), 78/174 (2026). 21% first disclosed by the model's maker; closed models named 108 vs open-weight 23 (a provider-visibility artifact); ~70% single-source. Counts reports, not attacks. Engineering takeaways: agent-driven secret hunting in public repos, AI-provider keys as crown jewels, detection tuned to machine pace. JSON/CSV downloadable.

entries.title: FreeToken: serving frontier MoE models on consumer GPUs
entries.by: Yang et al. with Keutzer, Han, Zaharia, Stoica, arXiv 2608.16157, and the FlashML-org/FreeToken repo, shared by Pallavi Ahuja
entries.summary: Edge-native MoE engine that treats GPU, CPU, host RAM and PCIe as one pool: double-buffered layer streaming in prefill, a q* policy splitting decode cache misses between GPU cache fill and direct CPU execution by measured host bandwidth, shared LRU expert cache, VRAM moved between experts and KV at runtime, and state checkpoints anchored at thinking/tool-call boundaries so harness context edits resume instead of recompute. Reported: 1.5-2.3x decode over llama.cpp/Ollama/KTransformers on an RTX 5090, worst TTFT under 44 s vs 150 s+ baselines, 35B at 39 tok/s on an 8 GB laptop, 284B on a gaming desktop, 753B GLM-5.2 on one workstation GPU.

entries.title: 20 open-source tools for AI agent security, checked
entries.by: Maryam Miradi's LinkedIn post, 2026-11-06: 20 tools in five groups of four
entries.summary: Guardrails (NeMo Guardrails, LLM Guard, AgentGuard, Guardian), red teaming (Promptfoo, garak, PyRIT, Giskard), authorization (OPA, OpenFGA, Cedar, Casbin), isolation (Firecracker, E2B, Kata, gVisor), data and supply chain (Presidio, Trivy, Semgrep, ModelScan). 16 of 20 healthy; LLM Guard is archived (as are Azure/PyRIT and Rebuff; PyRIT lives on at microsoft/PyRIT); AgentGuard and Guardian are ambiguous low-traction names; Trivy, Semgrep and ModelScan are build-time, not runtime. The summary orders the groups along one tool call's path and argues the deterministic layers (policy at the tool boundary, failing closed, and VM-grade isolation) must hold when the model is compromised; guardrail classifiers are noise reduction. Missing: credential brokering outside the sandbox, default-deny egress, audit trail, MCP tool-poisoning scans (snyk/agent-scan), PurpleLlama.

entries.title: SRE-1: an RL-trained 27B model for production incident investigation
entries.by: ResolveAI Labs paper, 2026-11-18; lead researchers Sean Bell and Dhruv Mahajan
entries.summary: Qwen3.8-27B RL-trained for 200 steps (modified CISPO, no KL, ratio mask [0.2, 5]) on 1,503 real incidents plus replays, synthetic and vendor environments, through 400+ live tools across about 60 integrations, every call pinned to alert time (they still caught an agent fetching its own fix). Output is a cited causal chain scored by one of 13 frontier judges against a reference built by an audited multi-agent labeler (as good as experts on 26 of 27). Live test, 49 cases: 6.9% base to 38.8% for one investigation; a five-run ensemble hits 71%, matching Fable 5.2 at 37% less cost; Opus 5.5 five-run 65% at 4.5x cost. Offline, 73 problems: pass 51.7% vs Opus 5.5 44.5% and Fable 5.2 39.0%, but mean scores nearly tie (0.749/0.743/0.731). The ablations are the real lesson: a 25k tool-output cap (+0.16), reserving room for the final answer (+0.14) and temperature 1 (+0.12) beat every reward tweak, and a bf16 gradient-accumulation bug beat twenty reward changes. Caveats: internal evals only, test pool skewed toward cases the frontier-backed product missed, judge-defined success, uneven baseline rollout counts in SRE-1's own harness, 1,503 vs 1,549 incident count unexplained. Walks back R031's multi-agent claim: the shipped model is a single agent; the swarm became the labeler.

entries.title: GPT-6.2 stops caching the Responses instructions field: where harnesses put the system prompt
entries.by: OpenCode v2.3.2 changelog, opencode issue #64550 and openai/codex issue #62312; surfaced by André Lindenberg
entries.summary: GPT-6.2 Sol/Astra place top-level `instructions` at the end of the input and never cache it (OpenAI reportedly confirmed it is deliberate); the same text as a leading developer message caches from step 2. Measured: 10.1k-token prompt 0 cached vs 10,113 cached; review sessions 2.85x the cost of GPT-6.1; both API-key and ChatGPT auth affected; OpenAI cache diagnostics report cache_hit while usage shows 0. OpenCode now sends a leading developer message on every Responses route (OpenAI, Copilot, Azure, OpenRouter). Lesson: request shape is a cost control; alert on cached-token share after model or SDK changes.

entries.title: Self-Disagreement: training models to hold a correct answer under pushback
entries.by: Abbasloo and Cheng, Microsoft Research, arXiv 2611.17563, 2026-11-12; shared by Pascal Biese
entries.summary: Models give up correct answers under wrong counter-arguments, and accuracy training, self-reflection, voting and SCoRe don't fix it: holding vs yielding is a separate 'dialectical competence'. The model states an answer, writes the strongest case against it without the reference, rules on it, and is rewarded with RLVR, the same exact-match check scoring the ruling (no second model, reward model or labels). Capitulation falls 25.3 pp (Qwen3-8B) and 36.1 pp (Gemma-2 9B) vs eleven frontier challengers; Gemma 3 12B from 20.2% to 2.6%; first-answer accuracy holds. Limits: checkable answers only, single-round, and acceptance of correct challenges drops too.

entries.title: Beacon: cross-harness session capture distilled into reviewed agent memory
entries.by: Asymptote Labs, agent-beacon, MIT, Go; shared by the AI Engineering LinkedIn page
entries.summary: An endpoint agent records sessions from 25+ harnesses (plus claude.ai/ChatGPT browser chat, cloud agents, CI) into one OpenTelemetry-shaped JSONL log. The "self-improving" loop is assisted curation: a hosted evaluator scores traces (candidate at task_success >= 0.50, mean >= 0.60), the running agent drafts the lesson from the trace, a human approves, and it is promoted to a plain Agent Skill any harness loads. Gaps: lessons carry no scope, expiry or evidence link; the installer preselects Beacon Cloud.

entries.title: SelfGraph: versioned knowledge graphs that tell an agent what they can't answer
entries.by: hydra-db/selfgraph README, Apache-2.0, early repo; surfaced by André Lindenberg
entries.summary: Python/TS SDK, CLI and MCP server over Neo4j, Memgraph, FalkorDB, HydraDB or embedded Kuzu: text or facts in, versioned graph out. Newer facts retire older ones without deletion; query as_of a date or as known then, so a backdated correction does not rewrite past answers (bitemporal). Ontology types, synonyms and certified definitions feed an LLM-free check_answerable that lists ungroundable terms before the agent answers. No vector store by default (BM25 + synonyms, BFS/PageRank walk). One level option ladders every capability from free/deterministic to LLM-backed, escalating only undecided cases.

entries.title: AtlasKV: billion-triple knowledge graphs inside attention, not in the prompt
entries.by: Huang et al., HKUST and Huawei, arXiv 2510.17934, v1 Oct 2025, v2 Apr 2026; resurfaced by Charly Wargnier
entries.summary: Parametric alternative to RAG in the KBLaM line: KG2KV encodes triples as key-value pairs injected into self-attention; HiKVP prunes a knowledge hierarchy so ~1B triples fit in under 20 GB VRAM, most KVs in CPU RAM. No retriever, no retrieved text in context, no retraining for new facts. Limits: flattened triples weaken multi-hop, top-k precision vs scale, CPU-GPU transfer latency; needs open weights, loses citation provenance. The 'RAG is dead' framing overstates a year-old result.

entries.title: Inside an AI-run AWS intrusion: 56 API calls in 141 ms and 78 alerts nobody escalated
entries.by: Boussaden, Porras Blanch and DeJesus, Elastic Security Labs, 13 Nov 2026
entries.summary: A CyberStrikeAI-driven intrusion across 8 identities in 4 AWS accounts, Sep 30 to Oct 16, 2026: machine-speed enumeration (56 userData calls in 141 ms), SSM parameter read then SendCommand 29 s later, and 78 medium/low alerts across 6 rules that were only linkable by source IP. Lesson: per-alert severity misses agent-speed campaigns; correlate on tempo and shared infrastructure.

entries.title: MLX Model Scout: a local agent team that never does the arithmetic
entries.by: michaelhannecke/mlx-model-scout (MIT), an agent-engineering course capstone; shared by Paul Iusztin
entries.summary: An MCP server whose planner, scout, analyst and advisor agents run on a local LLM, while a deterministic calculator produces every memory and tok/s figure (within a few percent of measured on an M5 Pro) and two server-enforced checkpoints gate the report. Useful pattern: numbers in code, LLM output validated against its inputs, flat schemas for small models.

entries.title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): when the CPU, not the image, decides exposure
entries.by: Oracle November 2026 CPU advisory and Horizon3 summary, via a platform write-up by Deepak Kumar
entries.summary: A HotSpot AVX-512 Base64 intrinsic writes 62-63 bytes past a heap array on malformed padding; reported pre-auth RCE in Keycloak, Jira, Jenkins and others. Exposure depends on the host CPU (AVX-512 VBMI), so one container image can be vulnerable on some node pools only; October-patched builds are still affected; pods must restart.

entries.title: GUARD: self-improving harnesses that only keep edits that don't break things
entries.by: Zhang, Kang et al., Google Cloud, arXiv 2611.23476, 2026-11-17; shared by Elvis Saravia
entries.summary: Frozen model, self-edited harness; a pre-execution checklist per task, paired regret that ranks newly broken criteria first and pins mastered ones, group-relative scoring of parallel candidate edits, and a gate that promotes only net-positive edits. 80.8% on 43 SDK tasks (+8.89 over start, +6.28 over Meta-Harness, 54.5% fewer tokens); zero procedural memory pollution where aggressive rewriters tripled it.

entries.title: Microsoft's Foundry Skill: a vendor ships its platform knowledge to rival coding agents
entries.by: Microsoft Foundry Blog, Foundry Dev Pack GA at Ignite, 2026-11-18; analysis by Rick Hightower
entries.summary: One install brings the azd ai CLI and a Foundry Skill that Microsoft lists for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor and other hosts: platform know-how and deterministic CLI workflows as one portable skill. Token savings claimed, not measured; a skill that issues commands runs them on your subscription, so read, pin and scope it.

entries.title: Linger and PolyStrata: a local personal agent on MoE experts tiered across GPU, RAM and SSD
entries.by: simplexai-labs/linger and PolyStrata (Apache-based custom license); shared by Charly Wargnier
entries.summary: PolyStrata keeps hot MoE experts on the GPU, warm ones in RAM, cold ones on SSD, promoting on use; claims a 125B 2-bit MoE at ~45 tok/s on a 12 GB RTX 3060 with 64 GB RAM. Linger adds nightly wiki memory, approval-gated proactive actions and nightly rule rewriting from user reactions. Many speeds are from simulated tiers; cloud-model parity claims are marketing-grade.

entries.title: pstack: a Cursor engineer's rigor playbooks for coding agents
entries.by: Lauren Tan, pstack in cursor/plugins (MIT); shared by André Lindenberg
entries.summary: One entry skill routes each task to one of 22 playbooks with verbatim steps; rules reject 'it compiles' or a self-report as proof, require citing the principles that shaped each decision, and push bulk work to subagents. Adversarial multi-model review, a committed decision log, and deliberately no planning skill ('the best spec is code').

entries.title: LangSmith Tool Gateway: identity, access and audit for every agent tool call
entries.by: LangChain blog, Karthic Subramanian, 2026-11-19 (public beta)
entries.summary: One URL in front of all MCP tools: curated tool kits per agent, search mode for large kits, per-call identity as the user (IdP, connect once, sign-in link mid-run) or as the agent (shared profile), deny and approval policies, and call metadata in the agent trace without payloads.

entries.title: Microsoft Agent 365: identities and traces for agents Microsoft doesn't host
entries.by: Microsoft Agent 365 and Azure Monitor Ignite 2026 posts; analysis by Rick Hightower
entries.summary: Entra Agent IDs for agents on eleven other platforms (preview, December), GA cross-cloud agent observability on OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions, and Foundry runtime controls outside the agent: egress allow/deny with audit mode, replaying handlers that need idempotent side effects, toolboxes holding downstream auth. Some items announcement-only; check status lines.

entries.title: TabPFN-4: a tabular foundation model that scales in-context prediction to 10 million rows
entries.by: Prior Labs technical report preview, 2026-11-19; announced by Frank Hutter
entries.summary: Sub-quadratic in-context architecture: 10M x 500 table in 38 min on one GPU versus extrapolated 65 h for its predecessor; ~300 Elo ahead of tuned baselines on 100k+ row tables; biggest gains on temporal and grouped data; trails one baseline on TabArena raw Elo. Vendor benchmarks, not yet released.

entries.title: Atto: retrieval embeddings from 840 parameters to 28 million
entries.by: David Mezzetti, NeuML, Hugging Face article, 2026-11-19
entries.summary: 30+ dense, sparse and ColBERT encoders on a conv-plus-attention mixer with hash embeddings, distilled from 110M teachers. An 840-parameter ColBERT scores 0.31 nDCG@10 on three BEIR sets; 950K matches 4M; a 14M dense model edges a 23M MiniLM. Watch output dimensions (up to 8,192) and narrow benchmarks.

entries.title: The Optimizely injection: a trusted script vendor serving malware to 178 organizations
entries.by: F5 blog on the 2026-11-16 Optimizely Web Experimentation compromise; shared by Ismael G.
entries.summary: A signup-flow flaw let attackers inject JavaScript that Optimizely's integration served to 178 organizations' visitors for ~16 hours: card skimming, wallet swapping, cookie theft. Allowlists, CSP and WAFs passed it because the source was trusted; behaviour monitoring plus field-level restrictions caught it.

entries.title: Codemod Workflow v2: the migration workflow becomes a TypeScript program
entries.by: Dev Agrawal, codemod.com blog, 2026-11-18; reshared by Alex Bit
entries.summary: Claim: in agent-driven code migrations the hard part is deciding when rules run, so dependency checks, per-stage file selection and approval gates move into a TypeScript workflow; resume reuses completed step results; transforms return findings instead of writing shared state. Vendor alpha.

entries.title: QDA: an agent designs the quantization recipe, scored by KL in minutes
entries.by: Li, Zhao, Han et al., MIT and NVIDIA, arXiv 2611.23388; shared by Elvis Saravia
entries.summary: Claim: a coding agent searching PTQ recipes beats the strongest public recipes by 0.9 to 2.2 points at 64 GPU-hours per search, because each candidate is scored in minutes by KL to the original model on hidden reasoning traces, with long-generation checks for loops and an evaluator kept outside the agent's sandbox.

entries.title: Safe Personal RSI: an update gate for a self-improving personal assistant
entries.by: arXiv 2611.23651 (CMU, UC San Diego, HKU, McGill, UC Berkeley and others); shared by DAIR.AI
entries.summary: Claim: a six-step gate (test, replay, undo-to-isolate, repair, decide, keep-current-on-failure) for prompt-only self-improvement rejected 20 of 21 risky updates; one repair cut attack violations from 10.7% to 0%, but a broad handwritten authority rule matched it.

entries.title: NVIDIA Dynamo for RL rollouts: routing, weight deltas and recovery
entries.by: Elmeleegy, Kim and Kranen, NVIDIA Technical Blog, 2026-11-19
entries.summary: Claim: RL post-training is gated by straggler rollouts, recomputed shared prefixes and weight refresh; Dynamo adds KV-aware routing that balances cache reuse against load, ModelExpress GPU-to-GPU and delta weight transfer, and worker recovery, while the RL framework keeps sample acceptance. Vendor; customer figures without baselines.

entries.title: Vercel Board: a message board as the coordination layer for coding agents
entries.by: vercel/board (Apache-2.0): README, factory template and Agent Factory guide; shared by André Lindenberg
entries.summary: Claim: each PR or task gets a thread where GitHub reviews, checks and Slack replies land; watchers wake agents, tasks are leased threads, agents post under their own name plus the credential owner, and the factory template merges only after human approval and green checks. Vendor-reported: over half of Vercel's PRs merged by its factory.

entries.title: Ready is not healthy: detect, mitigate and keep evidence for bad Kubernetes nodes
entries.by: ClickHouse engineering blog and node-problem-mitigator repo, Nov 2026; shared by Roopa Tangirala
entries.summary: Claim: at thousands of nodes on three clouds, Ready hides failed disks and hung kernels; split sensor (Node Problem Detector with durable conditions), actuator (a mitigator with a one-way evaluate, drain, terminate ladder, kill switch, rate limit, exclusions) and non-blocking evidence capture.

entries.title: SVReg: when a JEPA world model learns a latent map, and what it forgets
entries.by: Ren, Wang, Hoang, Kuang and LeCun (NYU, AMI Labs), technical report, Nov 2026; shared by Yann LeCun
entries.summary: Claim: a sliced variance floor instead of stop-gradient lets a next-frame JEPA learn smooth latent maps of mazes and city blocks with no position labels, but it can drop slow factors like object pose; Slow SVReg (slowness term plus gated residual predictor) keeps them and plans best on five control tasks.

entries.title: Serving Trace Lab: an interactive simulator for LLM batching and KV-cache memory
entries.by: Pallavi Ahuja, Serving Trace Lab (interactive simulator), 2026-11-20
entries.summary: Teaching tool: step an LLM server iteration by iteration to see prefill vs decode, static vs continuous batching, whole vs chunked prefill, and reserved vs paged KV allocation under memory pressure. Teach it by predicting finish times on one workload, then switching each policy.

entries.title: A Society of AI Scientists: 936 agents, 35 labs, and why review must execute code
entries.by: A Society of AI Scientists (MIT, Stanford and others), alphaXiv, 2026-11-19; shared by Ethan Mollick
entries.summary: Claim: over twelve weeks 936 agents in 35 labs published 936 code-and-data studies, retracted mistakes before upload and cited nulls as often as positives; text-only review could not tell disclosed from hidden flaws, while objections run as scripts overturned 49% of major-objection headline results.

entries.title: How the Claude Code team verifies agent-written code
entries.by: Addy Osmani, claude.dev blog, 2026-11-16
entries.summary: With about 90% of the team's code written and reviewed by Claude, verification is the bottleneck: a repo-local verify skill drives the real app end to end, property and differential tests supply independent oracles, three failed rounds escalate to a human, a 39-item diff-triggered reliability checklist runs only matching items, REVIEW.md is read from the base branch so a change can't edit its own checks, gates roll out in observe mode with every commit stamped by how it was verified, the reviewer is graded on past incidents with per-stage recall, and misses become pruned rules while flaky tests are root-caused or deleted.

entries.title: TrustGraph: access control before the model reads
entries.by: trustgraph-ai/trustgraph (Apache-2.0), release 2.10; shared by André Lindenberg, 2026-11-20
entries.summary: A self-hosted ontology runtime: OWL-guided extraction rejects triples that break domain, range or subclass rules, knowledge is stored as RDF with PROV-O lineage, and SHACL-AF policies are evaluated per node on every query (Allowed, Filtered or Violation) so restricted facts never reach the model; redacting answers afterward isn't access control. Served over MCP, SPARQL, REST and GraphRAG; open mode when no policies are loaded.

entries.title: Experience Rot: agents with memory stop checking changed tools
entries.by: Xu, Yin, Zhang, Zhao and Liu (eBay, University of Chicago), arXiv 2611.20922, 2026-11-16; shared by Pascal Biese
entries.summary: After a silent MCP-style tool change, agents that had done the task before copied their earlier call, even when the tool definition showed the change, and reported success (347 of 348 failures). Complete docs: 88-100% success with no experience vs 26-49% with stale experience; incomplete docs: about 23% stale vs 42% none. Worse with more experience (46% to 26% over 1 to 10 earlier tasks); every memory form affected; version notices and a system-prompt "check the docs" rule didn't help; reading back stored state before reporting raised success to 91%/69%. Hand-written histories hide the problem.

entries.title: Benchmark Factory: coding evals built from your own merged changes
entries.by: Shahidi, Poon, Xie et al. (Meta), arXiv 2611.18890, 2026-11-13; shared by Elvis Saravia
entries.summary: An agent loop sources tasks from landed production changes, runs models of known relative strength, diagnoses and repairs the sourcing query, prompt and grader until the benchmark clears label-free anchors (expected capability ordering within a margin, an informative difficulty band, low run-to-run variance), with a hash-split holdout that never drives repairs and human checkpoints for what it can't fix. Five cohorts; held-out configurations ranked as expected (60.6% vs 54.4%; 65.8% vs 60.5%), 9 of 10 per-cohort comparisons agreed; trivial benchmarks and five broken graders rejected; shuffled labels passed at most 1.4%.

entries.title: Codename MDASH: 9,791 AI findings filtered to 99 reports with fixes
entries.by: GitHub Blog (Ashley Wolf and Gregg Cochran), 2026-11-17; analysis by Rick Hightower
entries.summary: An agentic scanner flagged 9,791 possible issues in AutoGPT, Caddy, Express, FastMCP, ImageMagick and Netty; a Copilot-skills triage agent and then seven human researchers (about two days per project) cut them to 99 private reports with proofs of concept and suggested patches; 55 fixed and 14 released within days. The lesson is the ratio and who pays for the filter: ship fixes, not findings, and budget triage.

entries.title: Skills for Real Engineers: small, composable skills for coding agents
entries.by: mattpocock/skills (Matt Pocock, MIT); shared by Artem Kukharenko
entries.summary: Skills that encode classic practice for four agent failure modes: grilling interviews before code (misalignment), a shared domain glossary with ADRs (verbosity, naming drift), red-green-refactor TDD and gated debugging (broken code), and module-deepening architecture surveys (ball of mud); /to-spec and /to-tickets feed the issue tracker. User-invoked orchestrators may call model-invoked skills but never each other. Popularity, not measured outcomes.

entries.title: Copilot Evals and the Harnesses view: measuring the layer you change
entries.by: GitHub Changelog, 2026-11-17; analysis by Rick Hightower
entries.summary: Copilot Evals (/eval, Vally engine) runs repeatable evals of skills, custom agents and MCP tools, checking result and path, with before-and-after run comparison and per-run approval. The benchmarks site's Harnesses view compares Copilot CLI, Claude Code and Codex CLI on exact model pairs at medium effort, plotting resolution against cost with variance and bootstrap intervals; sound method, but GitHub measures its own product. Eval cases, not the runner, are the hard part.

entries.title: An unverified Lean-checked claim of the Riemann Hypothesis, and how to evaluate it
entries.by: Levent Alpöge, remark and Lean development, 2026-11-20; coverage by Scientific American; shared by Ethan Mollick and Elvis Saravia
entries.summary: Claims RH and GRH proved with Claude and formalized in Lean without extra axioms; only the Lean is released. Method sketched as a theta-lift analogue of Stepanov's multiplicity method. Unverified as of filing: the checklist covers statement fidelity, `#print axioms`, independent kernel checks and reproducible builds.

entries.title: CLI-Anything: generating a tested CLI for any app so agents skip the GUI
entries.by: HKUDS/CLI-Anything (HKU Data Intelligence Lab, Apache-2.0), arXiv 2606.03854; shared by André Lindenberg
entries.summary: A coding-agent plugin runs a seven-phase pipeline from source analysis to a Click CLI with `--json` on every command, a REPL, layered tests that call the real app, and a generated SKILL.md; community registry CLI-Hub. Tradeoffs: coverage limited to what the agent understood, upstream drift, generated tests checking generated code, registry supply chain.

entries.title: WorldTrace: keeping a world model's compressed KV cache addressable past its training horizon
entries.by: Wu, Elflein, Lucas et al. (NVIDIA, Princeton), NeurIPS 2026, arXiv 2608.07408; shared by NVIDIA AI
entries.summary: Past the training horizon, RoPE offsets leave stored frames unreachable and averaging rotated keys blurs them. Fix, training-free: a verbatim recent window plus summary slots at fixed in-range virtual positions, keys merged in un-rotated space, the model's attention choosing what to keep. +32.6% revisit similarity on the authors' LoopBench over a sliding window at equal budget, one 1.3B model.

entries.title: Posterior Matching Distillation: few-step image generation that keeps the teacher's diversity
entries.by: Yesiltepe, Berner, Vahdat and Yanardag (Virginia Tech, NVIDIA), arXiv 2611.26629, 2026-11-19
entries.summary: Reverse-KL distillation collapses to the teacher's dominant modes; PMD instead matches exponentially tilted posterior means, each one frozen-teacher call at a shifted input, and proves this identifies the full posterior. No auxiliary score network; one student serves any step budget on its grid. Best 4-step FID on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B per the paper; preprint.

entries.title: Hugging Face's own CDN: why model downloads break the web CDN model
entries.by: Thomas Wolf (Hugging Face), 2026-11-20, with the public CDN live-traffic page
entries.summary: Self-run since mid-2026: nearly 1 EB a month, ~80k req/s; snapshot 3.72 Tbps, 74.8% cache hit ratio, edge sites in AWS and GCP regions, not cities. Few huge objects pulled by GPU clusters, and launch-day floods on one model, invert web-CDN assumptions about placement, caching and capacity.

entries.title: METR's updated time-horizon report: fast progress on verifiable work, a gap on judgment
entries.by: MIT Technology Review (Grace Huckins), 2026-11-20, on METR's updated report
entries.summary: Adds longer and open-ended tasks with mostly estimated human times. Verifiable tasks keep improving exponentially; on judgment tasks (designing evals METR would use, scoring arguments) models still fall short, though the newest now reach borderline. Few such tasks, so trends there are uncertain.

entries.title: Cursor's incident: a read-only vendor key, credentials in agent traces, and a poisoned extension cache
entries.by: Cursor incident update, 2026-11-13; analysis by Steve Zenone
entries.summary: A read-only key held by the inference vendor exposed old coding-agent traces; unredacted credentials in a few traces led to SaaS tools, then to a credential that wrote malicious Claude Code extension builds onto Cursor's marketplace cache (about 11 hours, at most 5,000 users). Lesson: a read-only key is as safe as the data it reads; redact traces at capture, bind credentials to location, sign artifacts end to end.

entries.title: Adversarial distillation: how OpenAI protects reasoning traces, and what it may mean for open weights
entries.by: OpenAI, 2026-11-20; shared by Ethan Mollick
entries.summary: Students trained on exact reasoning traces gain more cyber capability than on summaries. Defences per request (adversarial training, input and output classifiers including tool-call arguments, reasoning bound to its conversation) and per campaign (account-network enforcement, shared indicators). Extraction success on Astra fell from 54.0% to 0.2%. Mollick's hypothesis that this slows open weights is unproven.

entries.title: Inkling 2 Mini: a looped 26B MoE built to run locally
entries.by: Thinking Machines Lab release, Hugging Face blog, 2026-11-20; shared by Merve Noyan
entries.summary: 26B stored, 3B active, multimodal, 1M context, NVFP4/MXFP8 experts plus a DSpark drafter. 24 physical layers, middle 12 looped three times with gated cross-pass messages, giving 48 layer visits from half the weights. Claims class-leading AAv5 and 32 of 48 benchmarks; a variable-loop research checkpoint trades passes for speed. Licence not stated in the blog.

entries.title: Sparse attention that pays off: eight hardware co-design guidelines for the indexer
entries.by: NVIDIA Technical Blog, 2026-11-17; shared by NVIDIA AI
entries.summary: Sparse attention moves cost into the indexer that scores every key (47% of a DeepSeek V3.2 prefill layer at 128K). Compares DSA, GLM, Qwen QSA, MiniMax MSA, NSA, MoBA and others; guidelines: tile-sized head grouping, FP16 epilogue, one key head, head dim 128, score fewer keys, fuse and reuse top-k, large blocks, large core-attention groups.

entries.title: Trail-code: team decisions as files in the repo, checked before every commit
entries.by: trailhq/Trail-Code (MIT); shared by André Lindenberg
entries.summary: A tree-sitter code map injected into prompts, plus Markdown learnings under .trail/learnings (Decided, Tried and ruled out, Watch out; touches list) committed with the code. trail check flags diffs that contradict a learning before commit; seeding mines past sessions and repeated PR review comments. Vendor-run results: 33 vs 27 of 50 SWE-bench Verified, 46% fewer tool calls in its own harness.

entries.title: Pro² Agent: research agents that track problems, not just code
entries.by: Chen, Peng, Tan et al. (Google, Johns Hopkins), arXiv 2611.25357, 2026-11-19; shared by DAIR.AI
entries.summary: The agent's primary state is a git-versioned Problem State, not the codebase: blocking problems with profiling evidence, each with candidate fixes carrying a [0,1] belief score and evidence; experiments are controlled tests that update importance and belief.
